citation.title: Analysis of neoclassical tearing mode stabilization experiment by electron cyclotron injection in KSTAR
citation.authors: M. Cha, M. Woo, S.-h. Hahn, Y.-S. Park, M. J. Choi, J.-K. Park, B.-h. Park, A. Rothstein, E. Kolemen, Y.-S. Na

topic: Offline analysis of 2/1 NTM stabilization by EC with PCS minimum-seeking control in KSTAR shot #31747 (2022 campaign)
own_question: Was the 2/1 NTM stabilized by aligned ECCD, as assessed with a simplified MRE in TRIASSIC?
actual_method_and_evidence: Single shot. Mirnov phase analysis and ECEI phase inversion were used to identify the mode. TORAY ECCD was computed on MSE-constrained EFIT equilibria. Simplified-MRE terms were computed offline. The paper reports that EC-related terms were negative after 7.3 s, when normalized misalignment was below 0.5. No CES ion-temperature data, nowcasting, or prediction validation is reported.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: KSTAR ECEI was used to infer electron-temperature fluctuation structure, including island phase inversion, in a 2022 discharge.
claim_checks.qualification: Electron diagnostic used for offline mode identification. It is not a calibrated Te input and not an ion or CES diagnostic. Figure not visually checked.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable; the paper has no temporal nowcast target. The PCS used boxcar-averaged n=1 amplitude; no latency figures are given.
validation_if_relevant: Only a single-shot interpretive analysis; no held-out data.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite as evidence on CES impurity Ti or nowcasting
Do not claim ECEI improves Ti estimation
Do not generalize to all KSTAR work
Do not treat MRE attribution as proven mechanism
Do not cite Wehner/Prater DOIs as this paper's DOI
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Only tangential: it is a KSTAR 2022 example of ECEI use and of real-time PCS control. It offers no grounding for the targets, inputs, or validation design. Exclude unless a brief ECEI-context citation is needed.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
